replacement: The emissaries of Pharnabazus and Tissaphernes negotiated separately, and a keen competition now arose at Lacedaemon over whether a fleet and army should be sent first to Ionia and Chios, or to the Hellespont. The Lacedaemonians, however, decidedly favored the Chians and Tissaphernes, who were backed by Alcibiades, the family friend of Endius, one of the ephors for that year. Indeed, this is how their house got its Laconic name: Alcibiades was the family name of Endius. Nevertheless the Lacedaemonians first sent Phrynis, one of the Perioeci, to Chios, to see whether the Chians had as many ships as they said and whether their city was generally as great as reported. When he brought word that they had been told the truth, the Lacedaemonians immediately made an alliance with the Chians and Erythraeans and voted to send them forty ships. According to the Chians, there were already not less than sixty in the island. At first the Lacedaemonians meant to send ten of these forty themselves, with Melanchridas as their admiral. But afterwards an earthquake occurred, and they sent Chalcideus instead of Melanchridas, and equipped only five ships in Laconia instead of ten. And the winter ended, and with it ended the nineteenth year of this war of which Thucydides is the historian.
